title: Chapter 7: Minghun
html:
“Fight poison with poison? Do you think we’re that easily fooled?!”

“Bro, just give me some money to fix my phone display and I’ll leave.”

“You think you can make this go away with a discounted ticket? No way!”

After several minutes of arguing, not one visitor showed any intention of entering the Haunted House. They remained firmly outside the gate as though crossing the threshold would be stepping into a minefield. Even Chen Ge could only sigh. “No one dares to try it? My Haunted House isn’t even scary. If you don’t believe me, check the reviews online.”

At that, several people in the crowd actually did.

“Indeed, all the reviews say the place is not scary.”

“The only good thing about it is apparently they hire a pretty lady to play the ghost.”

“Then, shall we give it a try?”

After another long wait, someone finally stepped forward. “What a bunch of cowards. It’s just a Haunted House—how scary can it be? I’ve seen plenty of cadavers. You think this will frighten me?”

The person who stepped forward was a young man with bushy eyebrows and a crew cut. At first glance, he looked completely ordinary.

“Bro, quit messing with us. There’s a limit to how much you can bluff.”

“How old are you? And you expect us to believe you’ve seen real cadavers?”

“We’re all scaredy-cats here, so why are you lying to us?”

As the mocking voices grew louder, a soft but firm voice cut through the noise. “He’s not lying. Working with cadavers is part of daily life for people in our field.”

The crowd turned toward the voice and saw a tall woman in a sun hat and white dress approaching from the park entrance. Her expression was cool and distant, as though the air around her had dropped several degrees.

“Senior!” The young man hurried toward her and reached for her bag, only to be stopped by an icy glare. He froze in place, flustered, with an awkward but polite smile on his face.

“Wait, did you just call her senior? You two are students?” Chen Ge’s attention shifted fully to the pair.

“We’re forensic science students at Jiujiang Medical University. I’m He San, and this is my senior, Gao Ru Xue.” The young man smiled at Chen Ge. “The video you uploaded last night was shared on our university forum, and after she watched it, Senior decided to come see this place for herself.”

“That unapproachable beauty studies forensics?”

“Her whole presence does suit the field, though.”

“Miss, how about we be friends…”

The male visitors began crowding around her. Acting as her self-appointed guardian, He San smiled. “I don’t think you understand what you’re getting into. My senior spends her mornings working with lab specimens, then goes straight to lunch without batting an eye. Last night she passed the anatomy lab, saw the preserved cadavers inside, and casually greeted them. Take my advice and know your limits. She’s probably examined more men in the lab than any of you have even dated.”

The unusual introduction achieved exactly what He San wanted: a two-meter-wide circle immediately opened around the woman.

Hearing the introduction, Chen Ge felt a sinking sensation. He had finally completed a Nightmare Mission and upgraded his Haunted House, only for his first challengers to be a pair of forensic science students. Their training meant their tolerance for frightening sights was naturally much higher than average.

“Can we go in now?” The woman strode impatiently up to Chen Ge. She was already tall, and in heels she stood nearly eye to eye with him.

“The regular ticket price is twenty, so with today’s fifty-percent discount, that’ll be ten. Before you go in, I need to give you a brief introduction and a warning.” Chen Ge remembered the black phone’s advice. Story and background were essential parts of a good Haunted House because they helped visitors immerse themselves in the experience.

“First, some background. A lot of online reviews say my Haunted House isn’t scary, but as a responsible owner, I should tell you a few things. Fifty years ago, this land was Jiujiang’s largest unmarked burial ground. Thirty years ago, the graves were cleared during urban redevelopment and Jiujiang City Hospital was built here. You can find what happened next online. After a series of unexplained incidents, the hospital was forced to close. My Haunted House was converted from one of the old hospital buildings left behind, and it still holds many secrets connected to that unfortunate place.”

Then Chen Ge pointed to the warning sign beside the main entrance. “Visitors with heart or vascular conditions should not enter. Visitors between twelve and sixteen must be accompanied by a parent or guardian at all times. If you don’t have any questions, follow me.”

Chen Ge pulled aside the heavy black curtains, closed the rusted gate, and led He San and Gao Ru Xue down the dark corridor.

“If they could not share a room in life, they would share a grave in death. This local legend has been passed down for generations.

“Ping Jianghou wanted to arrange a Minghun for her son, who had died young. She invited a fortune teller to examine his birth chart and fate, and eventually selected a girl she believed was the perfect companion for him in death.

“But the girl already loved someone else. To force her to comply, Ping Jianghou had the girl’s lover killed and threatened her parents.

“In the end, the girl agreed to marry a dead man to protect her family.

“Red wedding candles stood beside white funeral candles, joining a wedding and a funeral into one ceremony. The girl was sealed inside the coffin, and afterward strange events began to plague the Ping household.

“Bronze bird statues were said to weep blood, and paper dolls offered to the dead were seen blinking. Every midnight, a woman was said to wander the halls.

“The scenario you’re about to enter is called Minghun. The entire set is open for exploration, and you may go anywhere you like, but you must find the correct exit within fifteen minutes. If you want to surrender, stand beneath any surveillance camera and call for help. I’ll come get you.” Chen Ge stopped at the second-floor entrance and bowed. “Enjoy.”

“Sounds interesting, but if you think that’s enough to scare me, you’re sorely mistaken,” He San boasted shamelessly while hiding behind his senior. His mouth insisted he was not afraid, but his feet seemed rooted to the floor.

By contrast, Gao Ru Xue remained composed. She entered the scenario without a word.

“Senior, wait for me!”

Once the two visitors were inside, Chen Ge locked the entrance and called Xu Wan. “Xiao Wan, our guests are in. Get ready—and remember to put in your earpiece.”

After giving the necessary instructions, Chen Ge returned to the control room, where he could watch the surveillance feeds and operate the scenario’s mechanisms.

“I didn’t think I’d be using this track so soon. It does sound pretty dark, but these aren’t ordinary visitors, so I don’t have much choice.” Chen Ge switched on the sound system and put Black Friday on repeat.

With everything ready, he sat in front of the monitors and watched He San and Gao Ru Xue closely. If either of them ran into trouble, he would intervene immediately.
